verses.1:1: Solomon son of David established himself strongly over his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and magnified him exceedingly.
verses.1:2: Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of the thousands and the hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader of all Israel, the heads of the fathers' houses.
verses.1:3: So Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place in Gibeon, because there was the tent of meeting of God, which Moses, the LORD's servant, had made in the wilderness.
verses.1:4: However, David had brought the ark of God up from Kiriath-jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
verses.1:5: And the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there in front of the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought it.
verses.1:6: Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which belonged to the tent of meeting, and he offered up a thousand burnt offerings on it.
verses.1:7: In that night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I should give you."
verses.1:8: Solomon said to God, "You have shown great loyal love to my father David and have made me king in his place.
verses.1:9: Now, LORD God, let Your word to my father David be confirmed, for You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
verses.1:10: Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out before this people and come in; for who can judge this great people of Yours?"
verses.1:11: God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for riches, possessions, or honor, nor the life of those who hate you, and you did not even ask for many days, but asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself so that you may judge My people over whom I have made you king,
verses.1:12: wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. And I will give you riches, possessions, and honor such as none of the kings who were before you had, and after you there will be none like it."
verses.1:13: Then Solomon came to Jerusalem from before the tent of meeting at the high place that was in Gibeon, and he reigned over Israel.
verses.1:14: Solomon assembled chariots and horsemen; he had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.1:15: The king made silver and gold like stones in Jerusalem, and he made cedars like the sycamore trees in the lowland in abundance.
verses.1:16: The import of Solomon's horses was from Egypt and from Kue; the king's merchants would acquire them from Kue for a price.
verses.1:17: They brought up and exported from Egypt a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for one hundred fifty, and in the same way they exported them by their hand for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
verses.1:18: Now Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the LORD and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:1: Solomon numbered seventy thousand men as burden-bearers, eighty thousand men as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred overseers over them.
verses.2:2: Then Solomon sent word to Huram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with my father David and sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in—
verses.2:3: look, I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to Him, to burn fragrant incense before Him, and for the continual arrangement of bread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and at the appointed festivals of the LORD our God; this rests upon Israel forever.
verses.2:4: Now the house that I am about to build will be great, for our God is greater than all the gods.
verses.2:5: Yet who has the strength to build Him a house, since the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him? And who am I that I should build Him a house, except to burn incense before Him?
verses.2:6: So now send me a skilled man to work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue, and who knows how to make engravings, together with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
verses.2:7: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon; and see, my servants will be with your servants
verses.2:8: and to prepare timber for me in abundance, because the house that I am about to build will be great and wondrous.
verses.2:9: Now look, for the woodcutters who fell the timber, I will give your servants twenty thousand kors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand kors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
verses.2:10: Then Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them."
verses.2:11: And Huram said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, who has given King David a wise son, versed in insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingdom.
verses.2:12: Now I am sending a skilled man, versed in understanding, Huram-abi,
verses.2:13: the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan, while his father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold and silver, in bronze and iron, in stone and wood, and in purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and how to make every kind of engraving and devise every design that is given to him, together with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.
verses.2:14: Now then, the wheat and barley, the oil and wine, of which my lord spoke, let him send to his servants.
verses.2:15: And we will cut timber from Lebanon according to all your need, and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you will bring it up to Jerusalem."
verses.2:16: Then Solomon numbered all the men who were resident aliens in the land of Israel, after the numbering with which his father David had numbered them, and they were found to be one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
verses.2:17: He appointed from them seventy thousand as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to keep the people working.
verses.3:1: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where He had appeared to his father David, which he prepared at the place of David, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
verses.3:2: He began to build in the second month, on the second day, in the fourth year of his reign.
verses.3:3: Now these are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, in cubits by the former measure, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
verses.3:4: And the vestibule that was in front, its length across the width of the house was twenty cubits, and the height was one hundred twenty; and he overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.
verses.3:5: The great hall he paneled with cypress wood, and covered it with fine gold, and worked palm trees and chains onto it.
verses.3:6: He overlaid the house with precious stones for splendor, and the gold was gold of Parvaim.
verses.3:7: He covered the house—the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors—with gold, and he engraved cherubim on the walls.
verses.3:8: Then he made the chamber of the Most Holy Place: its length across the width of the house was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits; and he covered it with fine gold amounting to six hundred talents.
verses.3:9: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold, and the upper chambers he covered with gold.
verses.3:10: In the chamber of the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculpted work, and they overlaid them with gold.
verses.3:11: The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in length: one wing of the first was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub.
verses.3:12: And one wing of the second cherub was five cubits, touching the wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits, joined to the wing of the other cherub.
verses.3:13: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits; they stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
verses.3:14: He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and he worked cherubim onto it.
verses.3:15: In front of the house he made two pillars thirty-five cubits in length, and the capital on the top of each was five cubits.
verses.3:16: He made chains in the inner sanctuary and put them on the top of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and set them on the chains.
verses.3:17: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left; he called the name of the one on the right Jachin, and the name of the one on the left Boaz.
verses.4:1: And he made an altar of bronze; its length was twenty cubits, its width was twenty cubits, and its height was ten cubits.
verses.4:2: He also made the cast sea, ten cubits from its rim to its rim, circular all around; its height was five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits encircled it all around.
verses.4:3: And beneath it was the likeness of oxen all the way around, surrounding it, ten to a cubit, encircling the sea all around; the oxen were in two rows, cast in its casting.
verses.4:4: It stood upon twelve oxen: three facing northward, three facing westward, three facing southward, and three facing eastward; and the sea was upon them above, and all their hindquarters were inward.
verses.4:5: Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was like the workmanship of the rim of a cup, a lily blossom; it held and contained three thousand baths.
verses.4:6: He also made ten basins and placed five on the right side and five on the left side for washing in them; they would rinse in them what was prepared for the burnt offering, while the sea was for the priests to wash in.
verses.4:7: He also made the ten gold lampstands according to their prescribed manner, and he placed them in the temple hall, five on the right side and five on the left side.
verses.4:8: He also made ten tables and set them in the temple hall, five on the right side and five on the left side; and he made a hundred gold bowls.
verses.4:9: And he made the courtyard of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court; and their doors he overlaid with bronze.
verses.4:10: And the sea he placed on the right side, eastward, facing southward.
verses.4:11: Huram also made the pots, the shovels, and the bowls. Thus Huram finished doing the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:
verses.4:12: two pillars, the two globes and the capitals on the top of the pillars, and the two latticeworks to cover the two globes of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
verses.4:13: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranates for each latticework to cover the two globes of the capitals that were upon the pillars.
verses.4:14: He also made the stands, and he made the basins upon the stands;
verses.4:15: the one sea and the twelve oxen beneath it.
verses.4:16: The pots, the shovels, the forks, and all their utensils Huram, his master craftsman, made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, of polished bronze.
verses.4:17: In the Jordan plain the king cast them, in the thick soil between Succoth and Zeredah.
verses.4:18: And Solomon made all these utensils in very great abundance, for the weight of the bronze was not ascertained.
verses.4:19: Solomon also made all the utensils that were in the house of God: the gold altar, and the tables on which was the bread of the Presence;
verses.4:20: and the lampstands and their lamps, to kindle them according to the prescribed manner before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold.
verses.4:21: And the blossoms, the lamps, and the tongs were of gold—that is, the finest gold.
verses.4:22: And the wick trimmers, the bowls, the dishes, and the firepans were of pure gold; and as for the entrance of the house, its inner doors for the Most Holy Place and the doors of the house for the temple hall were of gold.
verses.5:1: So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was completed. And Solomon brought in the consecrated things of his father David; and the silver, the gold, and all the utensils he placed in the treasuries of the house of God.
verses.5:2: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the chiefs of the fathers' houses of the sons of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the city of David, which is Zion.
verses.5:3: And all the men of Israel assembled to the king at the feast, which was in the seventh month.
verses.5:4: So all the elders of Israel came, and the Levites lifted up the ark.
verses.5:5: And they brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils that were in the tent; the Levitical priests brought them up.
verses.5:6: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel who had gathered around him were before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen that could not be counted or numbered because of their multitude.
verses.5:7: Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD into its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, into the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
verses.5:8: And the cherubim were spreading out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim covered over the ark and its poles from above.
verses.5:9: The poles were long, so that the ends of the poles were visible from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, yet they were not visible outside; and it is there to this day.
verses.5:10: In the ark there was nothing except the two tablets that Moses put inside at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the sons of Israel as they came out of Egypt.
verses.5:11: Now when the priests came out of the holy place—for all the priests who were present had consecrated themselves without keeping to divisions,
verses.5:12: and all the Levites who were singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brothers, clothed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, were standing east of the altar, and with them a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets—
verses.5:13: and the trumpeters and the singers joined as one to make a single sound heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and as they lifted up the sound with trumpets, cymbals, and instruments of song, and praised the LORD, "For He is good, for His loyal love is forever," then the house was filled with a cloud, the house of the LORD.
verses.5:14: And the priests were not able to stand to serve because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
verses.6:1: Then Solomon said, "The LORD said He would dwell in the dense darkness.
verses.6:2: But I have built an exalted house for You, and an established place for Your dwelling forever."
verses.6:3: Then the king turned his face around and blessed the entire assembly of Israel, while the entire assembly of Israel was standing.
verses.6:4: And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, God of Israel, who with His mouth spoke to David my father and with His hands has fulfilled it, saying,
verses.6:5: 'From the day I brought My people out from the land of Egypt, I did not choose a city from all the tribes of Israel to build a house for My name to be there, and I did not choose a man to be ruler over My people Israel;
verses.6:6: but I chose Jerusalem for My name to be there, and I chose David to be over My people Israel.'
verses.6:7: And it was on the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, God of Israel.
verses.6:8: And the LORD said to David my father, 'Since it was on your heart to build a house for My name, you have done well that it was on your heart.
verses.6:9: However, you shall not build the house; instead, your son who comes from your loins, he will build the house for My name.'
verses.6:10: And the LORD has established His word that He spoke, and I have risen in place of David my father and sit upon the throne of Israel, just as the LORD spoke, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, God of Israel.
verses.6:11: And I have placed the ark there, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with the sons of Israel."
verses.6:12: Then he stood before the altar of the LORD, facing the entire assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms.
verses.6:13: For Solomon had made a bronze platform and placed it in the middle of the court, five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high; and he stood on it, knelt on his knees facing the entire assembly of Israel, and spread out his palms toward heaven.
verses.6:14: And he said, "LORD, God of Israel, there is no god like You in heaven and on earth, keeping the covenant and loyal love for Your servants who walk before You with all their heart,
verses.6:15: who have kept for Your servant David my father what You spoke to him; and You spoke with Your mouth and with Your hand have fulfilled it, as on this day.
verses.6:16: And now, LORD, God of Israel, keep for Your servant David my father what You spoke to him, saying, 'You shall not have a man cut off from before Me to sit on the throne of Israel, only if your sons keep their way to walk in My law just as you have walked before Me.'
verses.6:17: And now, LORD, God of Israel, may Your word that You spoke to Your servant David be proved true.
verses.6:18: Yet will God truly dwell with mankind upon the earth? Look, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You, how much less this house that I have built!
verses.6:19: Still, turn toward the prayer of Your servant and to his supplication, LORD my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer that Your servant is praying before You,
verses.6:20: so that Your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where You said You would place Your name, to listen to the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.
verses.6:21: And listen to the supplications of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place; may You hear from the place of Your dwelling, from heaven, and as You hear, forgive.
verses.6:22: If a man sins against his neighbor and an oath is imposed on him to make him swear, and he comes under oath before Your altar in this house,
verses.6:23: then may You hear from heaven, and act and judge Your servants, repaying the wicked by putting his way upon his head and vindicating the righteous by giving to him according to his righteousness.
verses.6:24: And if Your people Israel are struck down before an enemy because they sin against You, and they turn back and confess Your name, and pray and plead for mercy before You in this house,
verses.6:25: then may You hear from heaven, forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and return them to the land that You gave to them and to their fathers.
verses.6:26: When the heavens are shut and there is no rain because they sin against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name, and turn back from their sin because You afflict them,
verses.6:27: then may You hear in heaven and forgive the sin of Your servants and of Your people Israel, as You instruct them in the good way in which they should walk, and give rain upon Your land that You gave to Your people as an inheritance.
verses.6:28: If famine occurs in the land, if pestilence occurs, if blight and mildew, locust and caterpillar occur, if their enemies besiege them in the land of their gates, whatever plague and whatever sickness there is,
verses.6:29: whatever prayer, whatever supplication comes from any person or from all Your people Israel, as each knows his own affliction and his own pain and spreads out his palms toward this house,
verses.6:30: then may You hear from heaven, Your established dwelling place, and forgive, and give to each person according to all his ways, whose heart You know—for You alone know the heart of the sons of mankind—
verses.6:31: so that they may fear You, to walk in Your ways all the days that they live upon the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.
verses.6:32: And concerning the foreigner as well, who is not from Your people Israel, when he comes from a distant land because of Your great name and Your strong hand and Your outstretched arm—when they come and pray toward this house,
verses.6:33: then may You hear from heaven, from Your established dwelling place, and act according to everything for which the foreigner calls to You, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name, to fear You as Your people Israel do, and to know that Your name is called upon this house that I have built.
verses.6:34: If Your people go out to war against their enemies by the way on which You send them, and they pray to You toward this city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name,
verses.6:35: then hear their prayer and their supplication from heaven, and uphold their cause.
verses.6:36: If they sin against You—for there is no person who does not sin—and You become angry with them and give them over before an enemy, so that their captors take them captive to a land far away or near,
verses.6:37: and if they take it to heart in the land where they were taken captive, and turn back and plead for mercy to You in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have acted perversely, and we have done wickedly,'
verses.6:38: if they turn back to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity where they were led captive, and pray in the direction of their land that You gave to their fathers, and the city that You chose, and toward the house that I built for Your name,
verses.6:39: then hear from heaven, from Your established dwelling place, their prayer and their supplications, and uphold their cause, and forgive Your people who have sinned against You.
verses.6:40: Now, my God, please let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
verses.6:41: And now arise, LORD God, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength; may Your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may Your faithful ones rejoice in what is good.
verses.6:42: LORD God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed one; remember the acts of loyal love of David Your servant."
verses.7:1: When Solomon had finished praying, fire descended from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
verses.7:2: And the priests were unable to enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD had filled the house of the LORD.
verses.7:3: And all the sons of Israel were watching as the fire descended and the glory of the LORD was upon the house; and they knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement, worshiped, and gave thanks to the LORD, "For He is good, for His loyal love endures forever."
verses.7:4: And the king and all the people were offering sacrifice before the LORD.
verses.7:5: King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep and goats; and the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
verses.7:6: The priests stood at their posts, and the Levites as well, with the instruments of song of the LORD that King David had made to give thanks to the LORD—"For His loyal love endures forever"—whenever David offered praise through their hands; and the priests blew trumpets opposite them, while all Israel was standing.
verses.7:7: And Solomon consecrated the center of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, for he presented the burnt offerings and the fat portions of the peace offerings there, because the bronze altar that Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat portions.
verses.7:8: And Solomon celebrated the festival at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very large assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt.
verses.7:9: And on the eighth day they observed a solemn assembly, because they had kept the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.
verses.7:10: And on the twenty-third day of the seventh month he dismissed the people to their tents, joyful and cheerful of heart over the goodness that the LORD had done for David and for Solomon and for Israel His people.
verses.7:11: So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the house of the king; and all that came upon Solomon's heart to do in the house of the LORD and in his own house, he carried out with success.
verses.7:12: And the LORD appeared to Solomon by night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for Myself to be a house of sacrifice.
verses.7:13: If I shut the heavens and there is no rain, and if I command the locust to consume the land, or if I send pestilence among My people,
verses.7:14: and My people, upon whom My name is called, humble themselves and pray, and seek My face and turn back from their evil ways, then I Myself will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and heal their land.
verses.7:15: Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer of this place.
verses.7:16: And now I have chosen and consecrated this house for My name to be there forever, and My eyes and My heart will be there always.
verses.7:17: And as for you, if you walk before Me just as David your father walked, and act according to all that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and My judgments,
verses.7:18: then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, just as I covenanted with David your father, saying, 'You shall not have a man cut off to rule in Israel.'
verses.7:19: But if you yourselves turn away and forsake My statutes and My commandments that I have placed before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,
verses.7:20: then I will uproot them from My land that I gave to them; and this house that I have consecrated for My name I will cast out from My presence, and I will make it a proverb and a taunt among all the peoples.
verses.7:21: And as for this house, which was exalted, everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has the LORD done like this to this land and to this house?'
verses.7:22: And they will say, 'Because they abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out from the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them; therefore He has brought all this calamity upon them.'"
verses.8:1: And it happened at the end of twenty years, during which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house,
verses.8:2: that Solomon built up the cities that Huram had given to Solomon, and he settled the sons of Israel there.
verses.8:3: Then Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and prevailed against it.
verses.8:4: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, along with all the storehouse cities that he built in Hamath.
verses.8:5: He built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities with walls, double doors, and bars,
verses.8:6: as well as Baalath, all the storehouse cities that belonged to Solomon, all the cities for the chariots, the cities for the horsemen, and all that Solomon longed to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the whole land of his rule.
verses.8:7: As for all the people who remained from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who were not from Israel,
verses.8:8: from their descendants who remained after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had not wiped out, Solomon conscripted them for forced labor up to this day.
verses.8:9: Yet from the sons of Israel, Solomon did not appoint any as slaves for his work; instead, they were men of war, commanders of his captains, and commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.
verses.8:10: And these were the chiefs of the appointed officers belonging to King Solomon, two hundred fifty, who held authority over the people.
verses.8:11: Then Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the city of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "A wife of mine will not dwell in the house of David, king of Israel, because those places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy."
verses.8:12: Then Solomon offered up burnt offerings to the LORD upon the altar of the LORD, which he had built in front of the portico,
verses.8:13: according to each day's requirement, offering up in keeping with the command of Moses for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, and for the appointed festivals three times a year: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Booths.
verses.8:14: Following the regulation of his father David, he stationed the divisions of the priests at their service, and the Levites at their posts to praise and to minister before the priests according to each day's requirement, and the gatekeepers in their divisions at every gate; for such was the command of David, the man of God.
verses.8:15: And they did not turn aside from the command of the king concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter or regarding the treasuries.
verses.8:16: Thus all the work of Solomon was set in order, up to the day of the founding of the house of the LORD and until its completion; the house of the LORD was finished.
verses.8:17: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth along the shore of the sea in the land of Edom.
verses.8:18: And Huram sent him ships by the hand of his servants, together with servants who knew the sea; they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, took four hundred fifty talents of gold from there, and brought it to King Solomon.
verses.9:1: Now the queen of Sheba heard the report of Solomon, and she came to test Solomon with riddles in Jerusalem, with a very large entourage and camels carrying spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke with him about all that was in her heart.
verses.9:2: And Solomon explained to her all her questions; not one matter was hidden from Solomon that he did not explain to her.
verses.9:3: The queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon and the house that he had built,
verses.9:4: as well as the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their garments, his cupbearers and their garments, and his ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD; and there was no spirit left in her.
verses.9:5: Then she said to the king, "True was the report that I heard in my land regarding your words and your wisdom.
verses.9:6: Yet I did not believe their words until I came and my own eyes saw; and look, half the greatness of your wisdom had not been told to me; you have gone beyond the report that I heard.
verses.9:7: Happy are your men, and happy are these servants of yours, who stand in your presence continually and hear your wisdom!
verses.9:8: May the LORD your God be blessed, who delighted in you to set you on His throne as king for the LORD your God. Because of your God's love for Israel to establish them forever, He has set you over them as king to carry out justice and righteousness."
verses.9:9: Then she gave to the king one hundred twenty talents of gold, spices in very great abundance, and precious stones; never had there been spice like that which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.9:10: In addition, the servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum timber and precious stones.
verses.9:11: From the algum timber the king made walkways for the house of the LORD and for the house of the king, as well as lyres and harps for the singers; nothing like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.
verses.9:12: And King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she requested, beyond what she had brought to the king. Then she turned around and went to her land, she and her servants.
verses.9:13: Now the weight of the gold that came in to Solomon in a single year was six hundred sixty-six talents of gold,
verses.9:14: apart from what the traveling traders and the merchants were bringing; and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land were bringing gold and silver to Solomon.
verses.9:15: And King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of hammered gold went onto each large shield.
verses.9:16: And he made three hundred shields of hammered gold; three hundred shekels of gold went onto each shield. Then the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
verses.9:17: The king also made a great throne of ivory, and he plated it with pure gold.
verses.9:18: There were six steps for the throne and a footstool of gold, fastened to the throne, with armrests on this side and on that side of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests.
verses.9:19: And twelve lions were standing there on the six steps, on this side and on that side; such a thing had not been made for any kingdom.
verses.9:20: And all the drinking vessels of King Solomon were gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were refined gold; silver was not regarded as anything in the days of Solomon.
verses.9:21: For the king had ships going to Tarshish with the servants of Huram; once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive, carrying gold and silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
verses.9:22: Thus King Solomon grew greater than all the kings of the earth in wealth and wisdom.
verses.9:23: All the kings of the earth kept seeking Solomon's presence to hear his wisdom, which God had placed in his heart.
verses.9:24: And they were bringing, each man his tribute: articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weapons and spices, horses and mules, a set amount year after year.
verses.9:25: Solomon possessed four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, together with twelve thousand horsemen; he placed them in the cities for the chariots and with the king in Jerusalem.
verses.9:26: And he was ruler over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines, and all the way to the border of Egypt.
verses.9:27: And the king made silver in Jerusalem like stones, and cedars he made like the sycamore trees in the lowland in abundance.
verses.9:28: And horses were brought out from Egypt for Solomon, and from all the lands.
verses.9:29: As for the remaining deeds of Solomon, the first and the last, are they not written in the accounts of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the vision of Iddo the seer regarding Jeroboam son of Nebat?
verses.9:30: For forty years Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel.
verses.9:31: Then Solomon lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David his father; and his son Rehoboam became king in his place.
verses.10:1: And Rehoboam went to Shechem, since all Israel had come to Shechem to establish him as king.
verses.10:2: And it happened when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it, while he was in Egypt, where he had fled from before King Solomon, that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
verses.10:3: Then they sent and called for him; and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
verses.10:4: "Your father made our yoke harsh; so now lighten your father's harsh service and his heavy yoke that he placed on us, and we will serve you."
verses.10:5: And he said to them, "In three more days, return to me." So the people left.
verses.10:6: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had stood before his father Solomon while he was alive, saying, "How do you counsel returning an answer to this people?"
verses.10:7: And they spoke to him, saying, "If you will be good to this people, and show them favor, and speak good words to them, then they will be servants to you always."
verses.10:8: Yet he abandoned the counsel of the elders that they had counseled him, and he consulted with the young men who had grown up with him, who stood before him.
verses.10:9: And he said to them, "What do you counsel that we return as an answer to this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke that your father laid upon us'?"
verses.10:10: And the young men who had grown up with him spoke with him, saying, "This is what you are to say to the people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, so you lighten it from us'; this is what you are to say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
verses.10:11: Now then, my father loaded a heavy yoke upon you, but I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I, with scorpions.'"
verses.10:12: On the third day Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam, just as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
verses.10:13: The king gave them a harsh answer, and King Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the elders.
verses.10:14: And he spoke to them following the counsel of the young men, saying, "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to it; my father disciplined you with whips, but I, with scorpions."
verses.10:15: Thus the king did not listen to the people, because a turn of events had come from God, so that the LORD might confirm His word that He had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
verses.10:16: And as for all Israel, because the king did not listen to them, the people replied to the king, saying, "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse! Each man to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David!" Then all Israel went to their tents.
verses.10:17: Yet as for the sons of Israel dwelling in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam ruled over them as king.
verses.10:18: Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, and the sons of Israel stoned him with stones, and he died. Meanwhile, King Rehoboam hurried to climb into the chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
verses.10:19: Thus Israel has rebelled against the house of David up to this day.
verses.11:1: Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, and he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen men who waged war, to fight against Israel to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
verses.11:2: Then the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
verses.11:3: "Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying,
verses.11:4: 'This is what the LORD says: You must not go up and must not fight against your brothers. Return, each man to his own house, for this thing has come about from Me.'" So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
verses.11:5: Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built cities for fortification in Judah.
verses.11:10: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are in Judah and in Benjamin, fortified cities.
verses.11:11: He strengthened the fortresses and placed commanders in them, and stores of food, oil, and wine.
verses.11:12: In every single city he placed large shields and spears, and he strengthened them very greatly. So Judah and Benjamin belonged to him.
verses.11:13: Moreover, the priests and the Levites who were in all Israel took their stand with him from all their territory.
verses.11:14: For the Levites left their pasturelands and their possession and went to Judah and to Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from serving as priests to the LORD,
verses.11:15: and he appointed priests for himself for the high places, for the goat idols, and for the calves that he had made.
verses.11:16: After them, those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.11:17: They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and fortified Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, because they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.
verses.11:18: Rehoboam took for himself as a wife Mahalath daughter of Jerimoth son of David and of Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
verses.11:19: She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
verses.11:20: After her he took Maacah daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
verses.11:21: Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and concubines, for he took eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
verses.11:22: Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as head, as leader among his brothers, because he intended to make him king.
verses.11:23: He acted wisely and dispersed some of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to all the fortified cities. He gave them provisions in abundance, and he sought a multitude of wives.
verses.12:1: When the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he had grown strong, he abandoned the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
verses.12:2: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had acted unfaithfully against the LORD,
verses.12:3: with one thousand two hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and the people who came with him from Egypt were without number: Libyans, Sukkiim, and Cushites.
verses.12:4: He captured the fortified cities that belonged to Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.
verses.12:5: Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the officials of Judah who had gathered to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD says: You have abandoned Me, and I too have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak."
verses.12:6: So the officials of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."
verses.12:7: When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them, and I will give them a little deliverance, and My wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
verses.12:8: Yet they will become his servants, so that they may know My service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands."
verses.12:9: So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house. He took everything. He also took the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
verses.12:10: Then King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place and entrusted them into the charge of the officers of the guards who kept the entrance of the king's house.
verses.12:11: Whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards would come and carry them, and then bring them back to the guards' chamber.
verses.12:12: When he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, so as not to destroy him completely; moreover, there were good things in Judah.
verses.12:13: So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. For Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen from all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
verses.12:14: He did evil, because he did not prepare his heart to seek the LORD.
verses.12:15: Now the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, for genealogical registration? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
verses.12:16: Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Abijah his son reigned in his place.
verses.13:1: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
verses.13:2: He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
verses.13:3: Abijah joined battle with an army of mighty men of war, four hundred thousand chosen men, while Jeroboam drew up battle lines against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty men of valor.
verses.13:4: Then Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
verses.13:5: Should you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave kingship over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
verses.13:6: Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
verses.13:7: Worthless men, scoundrels, gathered around him and proved too strong for Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and faint of heart, and he did not stand firm before them.
verses.13:8: And now you intend to stand firm before the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David, and you are a great multitude, and with you are golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
verses.13:9: Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of the lands? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.
verses.13:10: But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned Him. The priests ministering to the LORD are sons of Aaron, and the Levites are at the work.
verses.13:11: They offer up to the LORD burnt offerings morning by morning and evening by evening, and fragrant incense; the arrangement of bread is on the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps is to be lit evening by evening; for we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned Him.
verses.13:12: Look, God is with us at our head, along with His priests and the alarm trumpets to sound the alarm against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed."
verses.13:13: Meanwhile Jeroboam had sent an ambush around to come from behind them; so they were in front of Judah, and the ambush was behind them.
verses.13:14: When Judah turned around, look, the battle was against them in front and behind. So they cried out to the LORD, and the priests were sounding the trumpets.
verses.13:15: Then the men of Judah raised a battle shout; and as the men of Judah raised the battle shout, God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
verses.13:16: The sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.
verses.13:17: Abijah and his people struck them with a great slaughter, so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell dead.
verses.13:18: So the sons of Israel were subdued at that time, while the sons of Judah prevailed because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.13:19: Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured cities from him: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephrain and its villages.
verses.13:20: Jeroboam no longer retained strength in the days of Abijah, and the LORD struck him, and he died.
verses.13:21: But Abijah grew strong, and took fourteen wives for himself, and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
verses.13:22: Now the rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
verses.13:23: Then Abijah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years.
verses.14:1: Asa did what was good and upright in the eyes of the LORD his God.
verses.14:2: He removed the foreign altars and the high places, shattered the standing stones, and chopped down the Asherim.
verses.14:3: He told Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to carry out the law and the commandment.
verses.14:4: He removed from all the cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars, and the kingdom was quiet before him.
verses.14:5: He built fortified cities in Judah, because the land was quiet and there was no war against him in those years, for the LORD had given him rest.
verses.14:6: He said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and enclose them with a wall and towers, gates and bars. The land is still before us, for we sought the LORD our God; we sought Him, and He gave us rest on every side." So they built and succeeded.
verses.14:7: Asa had an army of three hundred thousand from Judah carrying large shields and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand from Benjamin carrying shields and drawing bows; all of these were mighty men of valor.
verses.14:8: Then Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with an army of one million and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.
verses.14:9: Asa went out to face him, and they drew up for battle in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
verses.14:10: Then Asa called out to the LORD his God and said, "LORD, there is no one beside You to help, whether the mighty or the one without strength. Help us, LORD our God, for we lean on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. LORD, You are our God; let no mortal prevail against You."
verses.14:11: So the LORD struck the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.
verses.14:12: Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar, and so many of the Cushites fell that there was no recovery for them, for they were shattered before the LORD and before His army. They carried off a very great amount of plunder.
verses.14:13: They struck all the cities around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD was upon them; and they looted all the cities, because there was much loot in them.
verses.14:14: They also struck the tents of livestock, captured sheep in abundance and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.15:1: Now as for Azariah the son of Oded, the Spirit of God came upon him.
verses.15:2: He went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: the LORD is with you as long as you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will let Himself be found by you, yet if you abandon Him, He will abandon you.
verses.15:3: For many days Israel was without the God of truth, without a teaching priest, and without law.
verses.15:4: Yet in their distress they turned back to the LORD, the God of Israel; they searched for Him, and He let Himself be found by them.
verses.15:5: In those times there was no peace for the one going out or the one coming in, for great tumults were upon all the inhabitants of the lands.
verses.15:6: They were crushed, nation by nation and city by city, because God threw them into tumult with all kinds of distress.
verses.15:7: But as for you, be strong and do not let your hands grow weak, because there is a reward for your work."
verses.15:8: When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he strengthened himself and cleared away the detestable things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities that he had captured from the hill country of Ephraim. He also renewed the altar of the LORD that was in front of the portico of the LORD.
verses.15:9: He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those sojourning with them from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, because people from Israel had defected to him in great numbers when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
verses.15:10: They gathered in Jerusalem during the third month of the fifteenth year of the reign of Asa.
verses.15:11: On that day they sacrificed to the LORD from the plunder they had brought, seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep.
verses.15:12: They entered the covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul.
verses.15:13: And anyone who would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, from small to great, from man to woman.
verses.15:14: They swore an oath to the LORD in a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with horns.
verses.15:15: All Judah rejoiced over the oath, because with all their heart they had sworn, and with all their desire they had searched for Him, and He let Himself be found by them. And the LORD gave them rest on every side.
verses.15:16: Even Maacah, the mother of King Asa, he removed from being queen mother, because she had made a repulsive image for Asherah. Asa cut down her repulsive image, pulverized it, and burned it at the Kidron Brook.
verses.15:17: The high places, however, did not disappear from Israel; nevertheless, Asa's heart was undivided all his days.
verses.15:18: He brought the consecrated things of his father and his own consecrated things into the house of God: silver, gold, and vessels.
verses.15:19: There was no war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
verses.16:1: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel marched up against Judah and built Ramah, in order to allow no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.16:2: Asa then brought silver and gold out of the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the house of the king, and he sent them to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who resided in Damascus, saying,
verses.16:3: "There is a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold; go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, that he may withdraw from me."
verses.16:4: Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel; they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the storehouses of the cities of Naphtali.
verses.16:5: When Baasha heard of it, he ceased building Ramah and halted his work.
verses.16:6: Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried off the stones of Ramah and its timber with which Baasha had built, and he built Geba and Mizpah with them.
verses.16:7: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and told him, "Because you leaned on the king of Aram and did not lean on the LORD your God, therefore the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
verses.16:8: Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a vast army with exceedingly great numbers of chariots and horsemen? Yet because you leaned on the LORD, He gave them into your hand.
verses.16:9: For the eyes of the LORD roam across all the earth to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is undivided toward Him. You have behaved foolishly concerning this, for from now on there will be wars against you."
verses.16:10: Asa grew angry with the seer and placed him in the house of the stocks, because he was in a rage with him over this. At that time Asa also oppressed some of the people.
verses.16:11: Now the deeds of Asa, from first to last, see, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.16:12: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa fell ill in his feet, and his illness was exceedingly severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but rather the physicians.
verses.16:13: Then Asa lay down with his fathers and died in the forty-first year of his reign.
verses.16:14: They buried him in his tomb, which he had cut out for himself in the City of David, and they laid him on the bier that had been filled with spices of various kinds, blended in a crafted ointment; and they burned an exceedingly great fire for him.
verses.17:1: Then his son Jehoshaphat became king in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
verses.17:2: He stationed military forces in all the fortified cities of Judah, and he stationed garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
verses.17:3: The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, for he walked in the earlier ways of David his father and did not seek the Baals.
verses.17:4: Rather, he sought the God of his father and walked in His commandments, and not according to the practice of Israel.
verses.17:5: So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand, and all Judah gave tribute to Jehoshaphat; and he had wealth and honor in abundance.
verses.17:6: His heart grew bold in the ways of the LORD, and furthermore he removed the high places and the Asherim from Judah.
verses.17:7: In the third year of his reign he dispatched his officials—Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah.
verses.17:8: With them were the Levites—Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, the Levites—and with them were Elishama and Jehoram, the priests.
verses.17:9: They taught in Judah, and the book of the law of the LORD was with them; they went around through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
verses.17:10: The dread of the LORD came upon all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, and they did not wage war with Jehoshaphat.
verses.17:11: Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat tribute and silver as a levy, and the Arabians also brought him flocks—seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred male goats.
verses.17:12: Jehoshaphat continued to grow exceedingly great, and he built citadels and storage cities in Judah.
verses.17:13: He had abundant supplies in the cities of Judah, and soldiers—men of mighty valor—in Jerusalem.
verses.17:14: This was their enrollment according to their fathers' houses: for Judah, the commanders of thousands—Adnah the commander, and with him were three hundred thousand men of mighty valor.
verses.17:15: At his side was Jehohanan the commander, and with him were two hundred eighty thousand.
verses.17:16: At his side was Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself to the LORD, and with him were two hundred thousand men of mighty valor.
verses.17:17: From Benjamin was Eliada, a man of mighty valor, and with him were two hundred thousand equipped with bow and shield.
verses.17:18: At his side was Jehozabad, and with him were one hundred eighty thousand equipped for military service.
verses.17:19: These were those who served the king, in addition to those whom the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.
verses.18:1: Now Jehoshaphat had wealth and honor in abundance, and he entered into a marriage alliance with Ahab.
verses.18:2: After some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people with him, and he urged him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.
verses.18:3: Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" He said to him, "I am just as you are, and my people are as your people, and we are with you in the war."
verses.18:4: Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "First, please inquire for the word of the LORD."
verses.18:5: So the king of Israel gathered the prophets—four hundred men—and said to them, "Should we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or should I hold back?" They replied, "Go up, and God will give it into the king's hand."
verses.18:6: But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not another prophet of the LORD here so that we may inquire of him?"
verses.18:7: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom to inquire of the LORD, yet I hate him, because he does not prophesy good about me, but disaster all his days—he is Micaiah the son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "May the king not say that."
verses.18:8: Then the king of Israel summoned a court official and said, "Quickly bring Micaiah the son of Imla."
verses.18:9: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were seated, each on his own throne, dressed in robes; they were seated at the threshing floor by the entrance to the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
verses.18:10: Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made iron horns for himself and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'With these you will gore the Arameans until you completely destroy them.'"
verses.18:11: All the prophets were prophesying in the same manner, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, and the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
verses.18:12: Now the messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Look, the words of the prophets with one voice are good toward the king. Please let your word be like one of theirs, and speak what is good."
verses.18:13: Micaiah replied, "As the LORD lives, whatever my God says, that is what I will speak."
verses.18:14: When he came to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth-gilead for battle, or should I hold back?" He replied, "Go up and prosper, and they will be given into your hand."
verses.18:15: The king said to him, "How many times must I place you under oath that you speak nothing to me except the truth in the name of the LORD?"
verses.18:16: He replied, "I saw all Israel scattered across the mountains like sheep without a shepherd; and the LORD said, 'These have no master—let each man return to his house in peace.'"
verses.18:17: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not say to you that he does not prophesy good about me, only disaster?"
verses.18:18: Then Micaiah said, "Therefore, listen to the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD seated on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing at His right and at His left.
verses.18:19: And the LORD asked, 'Who will lure Ahab king of Israel so that he will go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One was saying one thing, and another was saying something else.
verses.18:20: Then the spirit stepped forward, stood before the LORD, and said, 'I will lure him.' The LORD asked him, 'In what way?'
verses.18:21: He answered, 'I will go out and become a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of all his prophets.' Then He said, 'You will lure him and prevail as well; go out and do it.'
verses.18:22: So now, look—the LORD has placed a spirit of falsehood in the mouth of these prophets of yours, and the LORD has spoken disaster against you."
verses.18:23: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah approached, struck Micaiah on the cheek, and asked, "By which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak with you?"
verses.18:24: Micaiah replied, "Look, you will see on that day when you go into a room within a room to hide yourself."
verses.18:25: Then the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and bring him back to Amon, governor of the city, and to Joash, the king's son,
verses.18:26: and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and feed him bread of hardship and water of hardship until I return in peace.'"
verses.18:27: Micaiah replied, "If you truly return in peace, then the LORD has not spoken through me." And he said, "Listen, all you peoples!"
verses.18:28: Then the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
verses.18:29: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and enter the battle, while you wear your own robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they entered the battle.
verses.18:30: Now the king of Aram had given orders to his chariot commanders, saying, "Do not fight with small or great, only with the king of Israel alone."
verses.18:31: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel!" So they closed in around him to fight. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him, and God turned them away from him.
verses.18:32: When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from going after him.
verses.18:33: Then a man drew a bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints and the armor. So he said to the chariot driver, "Turn your hand around and take me out of the army, for I have been wounded."
verses.18:34: The battle grew fierce on that day, and the king of Israel held himself upright in the chariot facing the Arameans until the evening; and he died at the time the sun went down.
verses.19:1: Then Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned to his house in peace, to Jerusalem.
verses.19:2: Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Are you to help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? On account of this, wrath is upon you from the presence of the LORD.
verses.19:3: Nevertheless, good things have been found in you, because you have purged the Asherah poles from the land and have directed your heart to seek God."
verses.19:4: Jehoshaphat resided in Jerusalem; then he went out once more among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and turned them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.19:5: He installed judges throughout the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, for each city.
verses.19:6: And he told the judges, "See what you are doing, for you are not judging for man, but for the LORD, and He is with you in the matter of judgment.
verses.19:7: So now, let the dread of the LORD be upon you. Take care as you act, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice, no partiality, and no taking of a bribe."
verses.19:8: In Jerusalem also, Jehoshaphat installed some of the Levites and the priests, as well as some of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, for the judgment of the LORD and for disputes; and they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.19:9: He charged them, saying, "In this manner you shall act: in the fear of the LORD, in faithfulness, and with a whole heart.
verses.19:10: In every dispute that comes to you from your brothers living in their cities—between bloodshed and bloodshed, between law and commandment, statutes and ordinances—you shall warn them so that they do not become guilty before the LORD and wrath does not come upon you and your brothers. In this manner you shall act, and you will not become guilty.
verses.19:11: Now see: Amariah the chief priest is over you in every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in every matter of the king; and the Levites are officers before you. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with the good."
verses.20:1: It happened after this that the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and some of the Ammonites with them, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.
verses.20:2: Then some came and reported to Jehoshaphat, saying, "A vast multitude has come against you from across the sea, from Aram, and look, they are in Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi."
verses.20:3: Jehoshaphat grew afraid; he set his face to seek the LORD and called a fast over all Judah.
verses.20:4: Then Judah gathered together to seek aid from the LORD; from all the cities of Judah as well they came to seek the LORD.
verses.20:5: Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court.
verses.20:6: He said, "LORD, God of our fathers, are You not God in the heavens? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations; in Your hand are strength and might, and there is no one who can withstand You.
verses.20:7: Did You not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land from before Your people Israel, and give it to the seed of Abraham, who loved You, forever?
verses.20:8: They lived in it and built for You in it a sanctuary for Your name, saying,
verses.20:9: 'If calamity comes upon us, a sword of judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we will stand before this house and before You, for Your name is in this house, and cry out to You out of our distress, and You will hear and save.'
verses.20:10: And now, look at the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom You did not allow Israel to invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, for they turned aside from them and did not destroy them.
verses.20:11: And look, they are repaying us by coming to expel us from Your possession that You gave us to possess.
verses.20:12: Our God, will You not judge them? For there is no strength in us before this vast multitude that is coming against us, and we do not know what we should do, but our eyes are upon You."
verses.20:13: Meanwhile, all Judah was standing before the LORD, even their little ones, their wives, and their sons.
verses.20:14: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite of the sons of Asaph, in the midst of the assembly.
verses.20:15: He said, "Pay attention, all Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat. This is what the LORD says to you: 'As for you, do not fear and do not be terrified before this vast multitude, for the battle does not belong to you, but to God.
verses.20:16: Tomorrow go down against them. Look, they are coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, in front of the wilderness of Jeruel.
verses.20:17: It is not for you to fight in this. Take your stand, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not fear and do not be terrified. Tomorrow go out to face them, and the LORD is with you.'"
verses.20:18: Then Jehoshaphat bowed low with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD to worship the LORD.
verses.20:19: And the Levites from the sons of the Kohathites and from the sons of the Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with an exceedingly loud voice.
verses.20:20: They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they were going out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Trust in the LORD your God, and you will be made secure; trust in His prophets, and you will succeed."
verses.20:21: He took counsel with the people and appointed singers to the LORD and those offering praise in holy splendor, going out before the armed force and saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for His loyal love is forever."
verses.20:22: At the time they began with singing and praise, the LORD set ambushers against the sons of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah, and they were routed.
verses.20:23: The sons of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction and annihilate them; and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they each helped to bring destruction upon his companion.
verses.20:24: When Judah arrived at the lookout of the wilderness, they turned toward the multitude, and look, they were corpses fallen to the ground, and no one had escaped.
verses.20:25: Then Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil, and they found among them in abundance goods, corpses, and precious articles, and they stripped for themselves more than they could carry. They spent three days plundering the spoil, because it was so abundant.
verses.20:26: On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD; therefore they called the name of that place the Valley of Beracah to this day.
verses.20:27: Then every man of Judah and Jerusalem turned back, with Jehoshaphat at their head, to return to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.
verses.20:28: They came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.
verses.20:29: And the dread of God came upon all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
verses.20:30: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, and his God gave him rest on every side.
verses.20:31: Thus Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
verses.20:32: He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.20:33: Yet the high places were not removed, and the people still had not directed their heart to the God of their fathers.
verses.20:34: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, the first and the last, see, they are written in the record of Jehu son of Hanani, which was entered in the book of the kings of Israel.
verses.20:35: After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel; he acted wickedly in doing so.
verses.20:36: He joined in partnership with him to build ships to go to Tarshish, and they built ships in Ezion-geber.
verses.20:37: Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken down your works." So the ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.
verses.21:1: Then Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Jehoram his son became king in his place.
verses.21:2: He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
verses.21:3: Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, along with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
verses.21:4: When Jehoram had risen over his father's kingdom and strengthened himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the officials of Israel.
verses.21:5: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
verses.21:6: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.21:7: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, on account of the covenant that He had made with David, and just as He had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons always.
verses.21:8: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.
verses.21:9: Then Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all the chariots with him. He rose by night and struck Edom, which had surrounded him, and the commanders of the chariots.
verses.21:10: So Edom has been in revolt from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at that time from under his hand, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers.
verses.21:11: Moreover, he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and he led the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution and drove Judah astray.
verses.21:12: Then a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: 'Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
verses.21:13: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution just as the house of Ahab promoted prostitution, and have also killed your brothers, your father's household, who were better than you,
verses.21:14: look, the LORD is about to strike a severe blow against your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions.
verses.21:15: And you yourself will be in many sicknesses, with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the sickness, day after day.'"
verses.21:16: Then the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who were beside the Cushites.
verses.21:17: They came up against Judah and broke into it, and they carried off all the possessions found in the king's house, as well as his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.
verses.21:18: After all this, the LORD struck him in his bowels with a sickness for which there was no healing.
verses.21:19: In the course of time, when the end of two years arrived, his bowels came out because of his sickness, and he died in severe diseases. And his people did not make a fire for him like the fire of his fathers.
verses.21:20: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed unregretted, and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
verses.22:1: Then the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the raiding band that had come with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the older ones. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
verses.22:2: Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah daughter of Omri.
verses.22:3: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in acting wickedly.
verses.22:4: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for they became his counselors after his father's death, to his destruction.
verses.22:5: He also followed their counsel and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to battle against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead; and the Arameans wounded Joram.
verses.22:6: So he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds that they had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.
verses.22:7: Now Ahaziah's downfall was from God in his coming to Joram; and when he came, he went out with Jehoram toward Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
verses.22:8: When Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, he found the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers who were attending Ahaziah, and he killed them.
verses.22:9: He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria; they brought him to Jehu and put him to death. Then they buried him, for they said, "He is a son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." And the house of Ahaziah had no one able to retain strength for the kingdom.
verses.22:10: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal seed of the house of Judah.
verses.22:11: But Jehoshabeath the king's daughter took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and she placed him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, daughter of King Jehoram and wife of Jehoiada the priest—for she was the sister of Ahaziah—hid him from Athaliah, so that she did not put him to death.
verses.22:12: He stayed with them in the house of God, hiding for six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.
verses.23:1: In the seventh year, Jehoiada strengthened himself and took the commanders of hundreds—Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri—into a covenant with him.
verses.23:2: They went around through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah and the heads of the fathers of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
verses.23:3: Then the whole assembly made a covenant in the house of God with the king. And he said to them, "Look, the king's son will reign, just as the LORD spoke concerning the sons of David.
verses.23:4: This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you who come in on the Sabbath, from the priests and from the Levites, shall be gatekeepers of the thresholds,
verses.23:5: and a third shall be at the king's house, and a third at the Foundation Gate, while all the people shall be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.23:6: Let no one enter the house of the LORD except the priests and those of the Levites who minister; they may enter, for they are holy, but all the people shall keep the watch of the LORD.
