verses.23:7: The Levites shall surround the king all around, each man with his weapons in his hand, and whoever enters the house shall be put to death; and be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out."
verses.23:8: So the Levites and all Judah did according to everything that Jehoiada the priest had commanded. Each man took his men, those coming in on the Sabbath together with those going out on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
verses.23:9: Then Jehoiada the priest gave to the commanders of hundreds the spears, the shields, and the bucklers that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of God.
verses.23:10: He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, all around the king.
verses.23:11: Then they brought out the king's son, placed the crown and the testimony on him, and made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, "Long live the king!"
verses.23:12: When Athaliah heard the sound of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.
verses.23:13: She looked, and there was the king standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the commanders and the trumpets beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with musical instruments directing the praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and said, "Treason! Treason!"
verses.23:14: Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds who were appointed over the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her shall be put to death by the sword." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
verses.23:15: So they laid hands on her, and she came to the entrance of the Horse Gate at the king's house, and they put her to death there.
verses.23:16: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, to be a people for the LORD.
verses.23:17: All the people went to the house of Baal and tore it down; they shattered its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
verses.23:18: Jehoiada placed the duties of the house of the LORD in the hand of the Levitical priests, whom David had apportioned over the house of the LORD to offer up the burnt offerings of the LORD, as it is written in the law of Moses, with joy and with singing, according to the direction of David.
verses.23:19: He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD so that no one unclean in any matter would enter.
verses.23:20: He took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers over the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They came through the Upper Gate into the king's house, and they seated the king on the throne of the kingdom.
verses.23:21: So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; and they had put Athaliah to death by the sword.
verses.24:1: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah from Beersheba.
verses.24:2: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
verses.24:3: Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
verses.24:4: After this, Joash had it in his heart to restore the house of the LORD.
verses.24:5: He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and gather silver from all Israel to repair the house of your God year by year, and you must act quickly in the matter." But the Levites did not act quickly.
verses.24:6: So the king called Jehoiada the chief and said to him, "Why have you not required of the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the levy of Moses the servant of the LORD, and of the assembly of Israel, for the tent of the testimony?"
verses.24:7: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken into the house of God, and also all the holy things of the house of the LORD they had used for the Baals.
verses.24:8: Then the king commanded, and they made one chest and placed it outside at the gate of the house of the LORD.
verses.24:9: And they made a proclamation in Judah and in Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the levy of Moses the servant of God upon Israel in the wilderness.
verses.24:10: All the officials and all the people rejoiced, and they brought it and dropped it into the chest until they had finished.
verses.24:11: Whenever the chest was brought to the king's office by the hand of the Levites, and when they saw that there was much silver, the king's scribe and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, lift it up, and return it to its place. They did this day by day and collected silver in abundance.
verses.24:12: Then the king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and craftsmen to restore the house of the LORD, and also craftsmen in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
verses.24:13: So those who did the work labored, and restoration progressed in the work by their hand; they established the house of God according to its proper design and strengthened it.
verses.24:14: When they had finished, they brought the rest of the silver before the king and Jehoiada, and it was made into vessels for the house of the LORD—vessels for ministering and for offering up, dishes, and vessels of gold and silver. And they offered up burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually all the days of Jehoiada.
verses.24:15: Then Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died; he was one hundred and thirty years old when he died.
verses.24:16: They buried him in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good in Israel, and toward God and His house.
verses.24:17: Now after the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king. Then the king listened to them.
verses.24:18: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherim and the idols; so wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt of theirs.
verses.24:19: Yet He sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD; they testified against them, but they did not pay attention.
verses.24:20: Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and he stood above the people and said to them, "This is what God says: 'Why are you transgressing the commandments of the LORD so that you will not prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.'"
verses.24:21: So they conspired against him and stoned him with stones by the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the LORD.
verses.24:22: King Joash did not remember the loyal love that Jehoiada his father had done for him, but he killed his son. And as he died, he said, "May the LORD see and require it!"
verses.24:23: At the turn of the year, the army of Aram marched up against him; they came to Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people, and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.
verses.24:24: Although the army of Aram had come with a small number of men, the LORD gave a very great army into their hand, because they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers. Thus they executed judgments against Joash.
verses.24:25: When they departed from him—for they left him with severe illnesses—his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the City of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
verses.24:26: Now these are the ones who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
verses.24:27: As for his sons, how the oracle against him increased, and the rebuilding of the house of God—look, they are written in the commentary of the Book of the Kings. And Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
verses.25:1: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.
verses.25:2: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, only not with an undivided heart.
verses.25:3: Now when the kingdom had grown strong under him, he killed his servants who had struck down the king his father.
verses.25:4: Yet he did not put their children to death, but acted according to what is written in the law, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, "Fathers shall not die for children, and children shall not die for fathers; instead, each one shall die for his own sin."
verses.25:5: Amaziah gathered Judah together and stationed them according to fathers' houses, under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered them from twenty years old and upward and found them to be three hundred thousand chosen men able to go out to war, handling spear and large shield.
verses.25:6: He also hired from Israel one hundred thousand mighty warriors for one hundred talents of silver.
verses.25:7: But a man of God came to him, saying, "King, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with any of the sons of Ephraim.
verses.25:8: Even if you go, act, be strong for the battle; God will cause you to stumble before an enemy, for there is power in God to help and to cause stumbling."
verses.25:9: Amaziah said to the man of God, "And what is to be done about the hundred talents that I have given to the troop of Israel?" The man of God said, "The LORD can give you far more than this."
verses.25:10: So Amaziah separated them, the troop that had come to him from Ephraim, to go to their own place. Their anger burned intensely against Judah, and they returned to their own place in burning anger.
verses.25:11: Then Amaziah strengthened himself, led his people, went to the Valley of Salt, and struck down ten thousand of the sons of Seir.
verses.25:12: The sons of Judah also took ten thousand captive alive, brought them to the top of the cliff, and hurled them down from the top of the cliff, and all of them were smashed to pieces.
verses.25:13: Meanwhile, the men of the troop whom Amaziah had sent back from going with him to battle raided the cities of Judah from Samaria as far as Beth-horon; they struck down three thousand of them and took great plunder.
verses.25:14: Now after Amaziah returned from striking down the Edomites, he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up for himself as gods; before them he would bow down, and to them he would burn incense.
verses.25:15: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent a prophet to him, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of the people, which did not rescue their own people from your hand?"
verses.25:16: As he was speaking to him, the king said to him, "Have we appointed you a counselor to the king? Stop! Why should they strike you down?" So the prophet stopped and said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
verses.25:17: Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us look at each other face to face."
verses.25:18: Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thornbush that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' Then a wild beast that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
verses.25:19: You say, 'Look, you have struck down Edom,' and your heart has lifted you up to boast. Now stay in your house. Why should you provoke disaster and fall, you and Judah with you?"
verses.25:20: But Amaziah did not listen, for it was from God, in order to hand them over, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
verses.25:21: So Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looked at each other face to face at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
verses.25:22: Judah was routed before Israel, and they fled, each man to his tents.
verses.25:23: Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh and brought him to Jerusalem; and he broke down four hundred cubits of the wall of Jerusalem, from the Ephraim Gate to the Turning Gate.
verses.25:24: He took all the gold and silver, all the vessels found in the house of God with Obed-edom, the treasures of the king's house, and the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
verses.25:25: Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.25:26: Now the rest of the deeds of Amaziah, the first and the last, see, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
verses.25:27: From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent after him to Lachish and put him to death there.
verses.25:28: They carried him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.
verses.26:1: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.26:2: It was he who built Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king lay down with his fathers.
verses.26:3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem fifty-two years. His mother's name was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
verses.26:4: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
verses.26:5: He persisted in seeking God during the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; and during the days that he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
verses.26:6: He went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
verses.26:7: God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.
verses.26:8: The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame went as far as the entrance of Egypt, for he became exceedingly strong.
verses.26:9: Moreover, Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the Angle, and fortified them.
verses.26:10: He built towers in the wilderness and hewed out many cisterns, for he had much livestock, both in the lowland and on the plain, as well as farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he was a lover of the soil.
verses.26:11: Uzziah also had an army of fighting men who went out to war in troops, according to the number of their muster by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
verses.26:12: The total number of the heads of the fathers' houses of the mighty warriors was two thousand six hundred.
verses.26:13: Under their direction was a military force of three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, waging war with mighty power to help the king against the enemy.
verses.26:14: Uzziah prepared for them, for the entire army, shields, spears, helmets, body armor, bows, and slingstones.
verses.26:15: In Jerusalem he made machines, the design of a skilled designer, to be on the towers and on the corners to shoot arrows and large stones. His fame went out far and wide, for he was marvelously helped until he became strong.
verses.26:16: Yet when he became strong, his heart grew proud to his ruin, and he acted unfaithfully against the LORD his God: he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
verses.26:17: Then Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of valor.
verses.26:18: They stood against King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out from the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully, and it will not be to your honor from the LORD God."
verses.26:19: Then Uzziah grew furious, with a censer in his hand to burn incense; and while he was furious with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.
verses.26:20: Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned toward him, and look, he was leprous on his forehead! They rushed him out from there, and he himself hurried to go out as well, because the LORD had struck him.
verses.26:21: King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death, and he lived in a separate house as a leper, because he was cut off from the house of the LORD. Meanwhile, his son Jotham was over the king's house, judging the people of the land.
verses.26:22: Now the rest of the deeds of Uzziah, the first and the last, Isaiah the prophet, son of Amoz, has written.
verses.26:23: So Uzziah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He is a leper." And his son Jotham became king in his place.
verses.27:1: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. His mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
verses.27:2: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done, only he did not enter the temple of the LORD. Yet the people were still acting corruptly.
verses.27:3: It was he who built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and on the wall of Ophel he built extensively.
verses.27:4: He also built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests he built fortresses and towers.
verses.27:5: He also fought with the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed over them. So the sons of Ammon gave him in that year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand kors of barley. The sons of Ammon rendered this to him both in the second year and in the third.
verses.27:6: Thus Jotham grew strong, because he established his ways before the LORD his God.
verses.27:7: Now the rest of the deeds of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, see, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.27:9: Then Jotham lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and his son Ahaz became king in his place.
verses.28:1: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began reigning, and for sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, like David his father.
verses.28:2: Instead, he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; he also made cast images for the Baals.
verses.28:3: Furthermore, he burned incense in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, in accordance with the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed from before the sons of Israel.
verses.28:4: He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and beneath every lush tree.
verses.28:5: So the LORD his God gave him into the hand of the king of Aram; they struck him, took a large body of captives from him, and brought them to Damascus. He was also given into the hand of the king of Israel, who struck him with a great blow.
verses.28:6: Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred twenty thousand in Judah in a single day, all of them valiant men, because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.28:7: And Zichri, a mighty warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the governor of the palace, and Elkanah, second in rank to the king.
verses.28:8: The sons of Israel took captive from their brothers two hundred thousand women, sons, and daughters; they also plundered abundant spoil from them and brought the spoil to Samaria.
verses.28:9: Now a prophet of the LORD was there whose name was Oded, and he went out before the army coming to Samaria and said to them, "Look, in the wrath of the LORD, the God of your fathers, against Judah, He gave them into your hand, yet you killed them in a fury that has reached up to the heavens.
verses.28:10: And now you intend to subjugate the children of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female slaves for yourselves. Yet do not even you yourselves have acts of guilt against the LORD your God?
verses.28:11: Now then, listen to me and send back the captives whom you captured from your brothers, for the fierce anger of the LORD is upon you."
verses.28:12: Then certain men among the heads of the sons of Ephraim—Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai—rose up against those coming from the campaign.
verses.28:13: They said to them, "You must not bring the captives here, because you are intending to bring guilt against the LORD upon us, to add to our sins and to our guilt; for our guilt is great, and fierce anger is against Israel."
verses.28:14: So the armed troops left the captives and the plunder before the officials and the entire assembly.
verses.28:15: Then the men who were designated by name stood up and took charge of the captives. From the spoil they clothed all the naked among them—they clothed them, put sandals on them, fed them, gave them drink, anointed them, led every feeble one on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers. Then they returned to Samaria.
verses.28:16: At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria to help him.
verses.28:17: For again the Edomites had come, struck Judah, and carried off captives.
verses.28:18: And the Philistines raided the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah; they captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco and its villages, Timnah and its villages, and Gimzo and its villages, and they settled there.
verses.28:19: For the LORD humbled Judah on account of Ahaz king of Israel, because he had cast off restraint in Judah and had acted with grave unfaithfulness against the LORD.
verses.28:20: So Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him; he brought distress upon him and did not strengthen him.
verses.28:21: For Ahaz took a share from the house of the LORD, and from the house of the king and of the officials, and gave it to the king of Assyria, yet it was of no help to him.
verses.28:22: And in the time of his distress he acted even more unfaithfully against the LORD—he, King Ahaz.
verses.28:23: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus that had struck him, and he said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram are the ones who help them, to them I will sacrifice so that they will help me." Yet they became the cause of downfall for him and for all Israel.
verses.28:24: Ahaz gathered the utensils of the house of God, cut the utensils of the house of God into pieces, shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and made altars for himself at every corner in Jerusalem.
verses.28:25: And in every single city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked the LORD, the God of his fathers, to anger.
verses.28:26: As for the rest of his acts and all his ways, the first and the last, see, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.28:27: Then Ahaz lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, because they did not bring him to the tombs of the kings of Israel; and his son Hezekiah became king in his place.
verses.29:1: Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he began reigning, and for twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem; the name of his mother was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
verses.29:2: He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, in accordance with all that David his father had done.
verses.29:3: He himself, in the first year of his reign, in the first month, opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
verses.29:4: He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them into the eastern square.
verses.29:5: He said to them, "Listen to me, Levites! Now consecrate yourselves and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, and bring the defilement out of the holy place.
verses.29:6: For our fathers acted unfaithfully and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They abandoned Him, turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD, and turned their backs.
verses.29:7: Moreover, they shut the doors of the vestibule, extinguished the lamps, burned no incense, and offered up no burnt offering in the holy place to the God of Israel.
verses.29:8: So the wrath of the LORD came upon Judah and Jerusalem, and He made them an object of terror, of desolation, and of hissing, just as you yourselves see with your eyes.
verses.29:9: Look, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, our daughters, and our wives are in captivity because of this.
verses.29:10: Now I have it in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that His fierce anger may turn back from us.
verses.29:11: My sons, do not be remiss now, for it is you whom the LORD has chosen to stand before Him, to minister to Him, and to be His ministers and those who burn incense."
verses.29:12: Then the Levites stood up: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, from the sons of the Kohathites; from the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
verses.29:13: from the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; from the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
verses.29:14: from the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and from the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
verses.29:15: They gathered their brothers, consecrated themselves, and entered in accordance with the king's command, by the words of the LORD, to cleanse the house of the LORD.
verses.29:16: The priests entered the interior of the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and they brought out all the uncleanness they found in the temple of the LORD to the courtyard of the house of the LORD. Then the Levites received it to carry outside to the Kidron Valley.
verses.29:17: On the first day of the first month they began to consecrate, and on the eighth day of the month they reached the vestibule of the LORD; they consecrated the house of the LORD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
verses.29:18: Then they went inside to King Hezekiah and said, "We have cleansed the entire house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the table of the rows of bread and all its utensils.
verses.29:19: Also, all the utensils that King Ahaz cast aside during his reign in his unfaithfulness we have prepared and consecrated, and here they are before the altar of the LORD."
verses.29:20: King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the city officials, and went up to the house of the LORD.
verses.29:21: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering on behalf of the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah. And he instructed the sons of Aaron, the priests, to offer them up on the altar of the LORD.
verses.29:22: So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and dashed it against the altar. Then they slaughtered the rams and dashed the blood against the altar, and they slaughtered the lambs and dashed the blood against the altar.
verses.29:23: Next they brought the male goats for the sin offering forward before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands upon them.
verses.29:24: The priests slaughtered them and offered their blood as a sin offering on the altar to make atonement for all Israel, because the king had ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.
verses.29:25: He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, in keeping with the command of David, Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet; indeed, the command was from the LORD by the hand of His prophets.
verses.29:26: So the Levites took their stand with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.
verses.29:27: Hezekiah then gave orders to offer up the burnt offering on the altar. At the moment the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD also began, joined by the trumpets and the accompaniment of the instruments of David king of Israel.
verses.29:28: The entire assembly was worshiping, the singers were singing, and the trumpets were sounding—all of this continued until the burnt offering was complete.
verses.29:29: When they had finished offering it up, the king and all those present with him knelt down and worshiped.
verses.29:30: King Hezekiah and the officials also told the Levites to praise the LORD using the words of David and of Asaph the seer. So they gave praise with gladness, and they bowed low and worshiped.
verses.29:31: Then Hezekiah spoke up and said, "Now you have dedicated yourselves to the LORD; come forward and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and everyone with a willing heart brought burnt offerings.
verses.29:32: The count of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought came to seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs—all of these as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.29:33: As for the consecrated offerings, there were six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep.
verses.29:34: However, the priests were too few and could not skin all the burnt offerings, so their brothers the Levites supported them until the work was finished and until the priests had consecrated themselves, for the Levites were more upright of heart to consecrate themselves than the priests.
verses.29:35: There were also burnt offerings in abundance, together with the fat portions of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offerings; so the service of the house of the LORD was established.
verses.29:36: Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had prepared for the people, for the matter had happened suddenly.
verses.30:1: Then Hezekiah sent word across all Israel and Judah, and he wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh as well, to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to observe Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.30:2: The king, his officials, and the entire assembly in Jerusalem had consulted together to observe the Passover in the second month.
verses.30:3: For they were unable to observe it at that time, because the priests had not consecrated themselves sufficiently and the people had not gathered to Jerusalem.
verses.30:4: The matter was right in the eyes of the king and in the eyes of the entire assembly.
verses.30:5: So they established a decree to circulate a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba even to Dan, to come to observe Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem, for they had not observed it in great numbers as it was written.
verses.30:6: So the couriers went across all Israel and Judah with the letters from the hand of the king and his officials, and in accordance with the king's command, saying, "Sons of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so that He may return to the escaped remnant left to you from the grasp of the kings of Assyria.
verses.30:7: Do not be like your fathers and like your brothers, who acted treacherously against the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that He handed them over to desolation, just as you see.
verses.30:8: Now do not harden your neck as your fathers did. Give your hand to the LORD and enter His sanctuary, which He has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, so that His burning anger may turn back from you.
verses.30:9: For when you return to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion before those who captured them and will return to this land; for gracious and compassionate is the LORD your God, and He will not avert His face from you if you return to Him."
verses.30:10: So the couriers were passing from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, even as far as Zebulun, yet people kept laughing at them and scoffing at them.
verses.30:11: However, some men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
verses.30:12: In Judah as well, the hand of God was present to give them one heart to carry out the command of the king and the officials by the word of the LORD.
verses.30:13: Many people gathered at Jerusalem to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, an exceedingly vast assembly.
verses.30:14: They rose up and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem; they also removed all the incense altars and cast them into the Kidron Valley.
verses.30:15: Then they slaughtered the Passover offering on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites were put to shame, so they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.
verses.30:16: They stood at their posts according to their regulation, in keeping with the law of Moses the man of God, while the priests dashed the blood from the hand of the Levites.
verses.30:17: For there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves; therefore the Levites were in charge of slaughtering the Passover offerings for everyone who was not clean, in order to consecrate them to the LORD.
verses.30:18: For a majority of the people, many from Ephraim and Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, for they ate the Passover contrary to what is written. Yet Hezekiah prayed on their behalf, saying, "May the good LORD make atonement for
verses.30:19: everyone who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his fathers, even if not according to the purification of the sanctuary."
verses.30:20: So the LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
verses.30:21: The sons of Israel present in Jerusalem observed the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great gladness, while the Levites and the priests praised the LORD day by day with instruments of might to the LORD.
verses.30:22: Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites who demonstrated good insight for the LORD. So they ate the appointed feast throughout the seven days, sacrificing peace offerings and making confession to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.30:23: Then the entire assembly took counsel together to observe seven more days, so they observed seven days in gladness.
verses.30:24: For Hezekiah king of Judah set apart for the assembly one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials set apart for the assembly one thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and priests consecrated themselves in great numbers.
verses.30:25: The entire assembly of Judah rejoiced, together with the priests and the Levites, and the entire assembly that came out of Israel, and the resident foreigners who came from the land of Israel and those living in Judah.
verses.30:26: So there was great gladness in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, nothing like this had happened in Jerusalem.
verses.30:27: Then the Levitical priests rose up and blessed the people, and their voice was heard, and their prayer came to His holy dwelling place, to heaven.
verses.31:1: When all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and shattered the standing pillars, chopped down the Asherah poles, and pulled down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they made a complete end of them. Then all the sons of Israel returned, each man to his holding, to their cities.
verses.31:2: Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites according to their divisions, each man according to his service, for both the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to praise within the gates of the camps of the LORD.
verses.31:3: The king's portion from his own possessions was for the burnt offerings: the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, and for the appointed feasts, as it is written in the law of the LORD.
verses.31:4: He also instructed the people, the residents of Jerusalem, to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they might hold firmly to the law of the LORD.
verses.31:5: As soon as the word spread abroad, the sons of Israel abundantly supplied the firstfruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and all the produce of the field, and they brought in the tithe of everything in abundance.
verses.31:6: The sons of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of the sacred things that had been consecrated to the LORD their God, and laid them down in heaps upon heaps.
verses.31:7: In the third month they began laying the foundation of the heaps, and in the seventh month they finished.
verses.31:8: Then Hezekiah and the officials arrived and saw the heaps, and they blessed the LORD and His people Israel.
verses.31:9: Hezekiah then inquired of the priests and the Levites regarding the heaps.
verses.31:10: Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, spoke to him and said, "Since they began bringing the contribution into the house of the LORD, we have eaten and been satisfied and left over in abundance; for the LORD has blessed His people, and this great store is what remains."
verses.31:11: Then Hezekiah gave orders to prepare chambers in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them.
verses.31:12: They faithfully brought in the contribution, the tithe, and the sacred things. Over them as chief overseer was Conaniah the Levite, and Shimei his brother was second in rank.
verses.31:13: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were supervisors under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by appointment of King Hezekiah and Azariah, the chief overseer of the house of God.
verses.31:14: Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper on the east side, was in charge of the freewill offerings to God, to distribute the contribution to the LORD and the most holy offerings.
verses.31:15: At his side were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah in the cities of the priests, faithfully distributing to their brothers by divisions, to great and small alike,
verses.31:16: apart from those of them enrolled by genealogy, males from three years old and upward, for everyone who entered the house of the LORD for each day's requirement, for their service in their duties according to their divisions.
verses.31:17: The genealogical enrollment of the priests was according to their fathers' houses, and that of the Levites from twenty years old and upward was in their duties by their divisions,
verses.31:18: including enrollment with all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, for the entire assembly; for in their faithfulness they consecrated themselves in holiness.
verses.31:19: And for the sons of Aaron, the priests, in the pastureland fields of their cities, in city after city, there were men designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone enrolled by genealogy among the Levites.
verses.31:20: This is what Hezekiah carried out across all Judah; he did what was good, upright, and true in the presence of the LORD his God.
verses.31:21: And in every endeavor that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God, he acted with his whole heart and succeeded.
verses.32:1: After these acts and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and entered Judah; he encamped against the fortified cities and determined to breach them for himself.
verses.32:2: And Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that his face was set for war against Jerusalem.
verses.32:3: So he took counsel with his officers and his mighty men to stop up the waters of the springs that were outside the city, and they helped him.
verses.32:4: A large crowd of people gathered together, and they stopped up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the middle of the land, saying, "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find abundant water?"
verses.32:5: He strengthened himself and rebuilt the entire wall that had been broken down, raised it up to the towers, and built another wall on the outside; he also strengthened the Millo in the City of David and made weapons in abundance and shields.
verses.32:6: He appointed battle commanders over the people, gathered them to himself in the square of the city gate, and spoke to their hearts, saying,
verses.32:7: "Be strong and resolute; do not fear and do not be dismayed before the king of Assyria or before all the multitude that is with him, for there is more with us than with him.
verses.32:8: With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles." And the people relied on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
verses.32:9: After this, Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem, while he himself was before Lachish and all his power was with him, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying,
verses.32:10: "This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: On what are you trusting, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem?
verses.32:11: Is not Hezekiah misleading you to hand you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, 'The LORD our God will rescue us from the grasp of the king of Assyria'?
verses.32:12: Was it not this same Hezekiah who removed His high places and His altars and spoke to Judah and Jerusalem, saying, 'Before one altar you shall worship, and on it you shall burn incense'?
verses.32:13: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands at all able to rescue their land from my hand?
verses.32:14: Who among all the gods of these nations that my fathers utterly destroyed was able to rescue his people from my hand, that your God should be able to rescue you from my hand?
verses.32:15: And now, do not let Hezekiah deceive you, and do not let him mislead you in this way, and do not believe him; for no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to rescue his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God rescue you from my hand!"
verses.32:16: His servants spoke even more against the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.
verses.32:17: He also wrote letters to taunt the LORD, the God of Israel, and to speak against Him, saying, "Just as the gods of the nations of the lands have not rescued their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not rescue His people from my hand."
verses.32:18: They called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten them and throw them into panic, so that they might capture the city.
verses.32:19: And they spoke about the God of Jerusalem as about the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
verses.32:20: Then King Hezekiah and Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, prayed about this and cried out to heaven.
verses.32:21: And the LORD sent an angel who annihilated every mighty warrior, leader, and commander in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned with shame of face to his own land. And when he entered the house of his god, some of those who came from his own body struck him down there with the sword.
verses.32:22: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and He cared for them on every side.
verses.32:23: Many brought gifts to the LORD at Jerusalem and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah, and he was exalted in the sight of all the nations from that time on.
verses.32:24: In those days Hezekiah became ill to the point of death, and he prayed to the LORD; and He spoke to him and gave him a sign.
verses.32:25: But Hezekiah did not make a return according to the benefit bestowed on him, because his heart became proud; therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.32:26: Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so the wrath of the LORD did not come upon them in the days of Hezekiah.
verses.32:27: Now Hezekiah had exceedingly great wealth and honor, and he made treasuries for himself for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and every kind of desirable article,
verses.32:28: and storehouses for the produce of grain, new wine, and fresh oil, and stalls for every kind of livestock, and flocks for the folds.
verses.32:29: He also made cities for himself, along with flocks and herds in abundance, for God had given him very great possessions.
verses.32:30: It was this same Hezekiah who stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them straight down to the west side of the City of David. And Hezekiah succeeded in all his work.
verses.32:31: Even so, in the matter of the envoys of the rulers of Babylon who sent to him to inquire about the sign that had occurred in the land, God left him to test him, to know all that was in his heart.
verses.32:32: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his acts of loyal love, see, they are written in the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, the prophet, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.32:33: So Hezekiah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him on the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death. And Manasseh his son became king in his place.
verses.33:1: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:2: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had dispossessed before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:3: He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had demolished, erected altars for the Baals, made Asherahs, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
verses.33:4: He also built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem My name shall be forever."
verses.33:5: And he built altars for all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.
verses.33:6: He also made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom; he practiced soothsaying, divination, and sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He did much that was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.
verses.33:7: Then he placed the carved image of the idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to Solomon his son, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever;
verses.33:8: and I will not again remove the foot of Israel from the land that I appointed for your fathers, if only they are careful to do all that I have commanded them, according to all the law, the statutes, and the ordinances by the hand of Moses."
verses.33:9: So Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the sons of Israel.
verses.33:10: The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.
verses.33:11: Therefore the LORD brought against them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, and they captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze shackles, and led him to Babylon.
verses.33:12: And when he was in distress, he implored the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.
verses.33:13: And he prayed to Him, and He accepted his plea and heard his supplication, and He restored him to Jerusalem to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.
verses.33:14: After this he built an outer wall for the City of David west of Gihon in the valley, extending to the entrance of the Fish Gate; he ran it around Ophel and raised it very high. He also stationed army commanders in all the fortified cities in Judah.
verses.33:15: He also removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, along with all the altars that he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.
verses.33:16: And he rebuilt the altar of the LORD and sacrificed on it sacrifices of peace offerings and thanksgiving; and he commanded Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.33:17: Nevertheless, the people were still sacrificing at the high places, yet only to the LORD their God.
verses.33:18: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, see, they are in the records of the kings of Israel.
verses.33:19: His prayer also, and how his plea was accepted, and all his sin and his unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up the Asherahs and the carved images before he humbled himself, see, they are written in the records of Hozai.
verses.33:20: So Manasseh lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house. And Amon his son became king in his place.
verses.33:21: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
verses.33:22: He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Manasseh his father had done; and Amon sacrificed to all the carved images that Manasseh his father had made, and he served them.
verses.33:23: And he did not humble himself before the LORD as Manasseh his father had humbled himself; instead, this same Amon multiplied guilt.
verses.33:24: Then his servants conspired against him and put him to death in his own house.
verses.33:25: But the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made Josiah his son king in his place.
verses.34:1: Josiah was eight years old when he began reigning, and for thirty-one years he reigned in Jerusalem.
verses.34:2: He did what was upright in the eyes of the LORD and walked in the ways of his father David, and he did not turn aside to the right or to the left.
verses.34:3: In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year he began to purify Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the cast images.
verses.34:4: They tore down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and he chopped down the incense altars that stood high above them. He shattered the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the cast images, crushed them to powder, and scattered it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
verses.34:5: He also burned the bones of priests upon their altars, and he purified Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:6: And in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, even as far as Naphtali, in their ruins on every side,
verses.34:7: he tore down the altars, pounded the Asherah poles and the carved images to powder, and chopped down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:8: In the eighteenth year of his reign, in purifying the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.
verses.34:9: They came to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, had collected from the hand of Manasseh and Ephraim, from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin; and they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.34:10: They put it into the hand of the workmen who had oversight in the house of the LORD, and the workmen who were working in the house of the LORD gave it to mend and repair the house.
verses.34:11: They gave it to the craftsmen and the builders to buy quarried stone and timber for binders, and to lay beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had ruined.
verses.34:12: The men carried out the work faithfully. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites from the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the sons of the Kohathites, to supervise. And the Levites, all who were skilled with musical instruments,
verses.34:13: were over the burden-bearers and supervised everyone doing work for every kind of service; and some of the Levites were scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
verses.34:14: While they were taking out the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the book of the law of the LORD given by the hand of Moses.
verses.34:15: Hilkiah spoke up and said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.
verses.34:16: Shaphan brought the book to the king, and he also brought back word to the king, saying, "Everything that was placed into the hand of your servants, they are doing.
verses.34:17: They have poured out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and have put it into the hand of the overseers and into the hand of the workmen."
verses.34:18: Then Shaphan the scribe informed the king, saying, "Hilkiah the priest gave me a book." And Shaphan read from it in the presence of the king.
verses.34:19: Now when the king heard the words of the law, he tore his garments.
verses.34:20: Then the king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the servant of the king, saying,
verses.34:21: "Go, inquire of the LORD on my behalf and on behalf of those who remain in Israel and in Judah concerning the words of the book that was found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that has been poured out on us, because our fathers did not keep the word of the LORD, to act in accordance with all that is written in this book."
verses.34:22: So Hilkiah and those whom the king had sent went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the garments—now she lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter—and they spoke to her to this effect.
verses.34:23: She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me,
verses.34:24: 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am bringing disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the curses written in the book that they read before the king of Judah.
verses.34:25: Because they have forsaken Me and have burned incense to other gods, in order to provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands, My wrath will be poured out on this place and will not be quenched.'
verses.34:26: But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD, thus you are to say to him: 'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: As for the words that you have heard,
verses.34:27: because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words against this place and against its inhabitants, and you humbled yourself before Me, tore your garments, and wept before Me, I also have heard, declares the LORD.
verses.34:28: Look, I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace; your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am bringing upon this place and upon its inhabitants.'" So they brought back word to the king.
verses.34:29: The king then sent out and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.34:30: The king went up to the house of the LORD, together with all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the least. And he read in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
verses.34:31: Then the king stood in his place and made the covenant before the LORD, to walk after the LORD and to keep His commandments, His testimonies, and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to carry out the words of the covenant that were written in this book.
verses.34:32: Moreover, he made all who were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand by it; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.
verses.34:33: Josiah removed all the abominations from all the lands belonging to the sons of Israel, and he made all who were present in Israel serve the LORD their God. Throughout all his days they did not turn aside from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.
verses.35:1: Josiah observed a Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover offering on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.35:2: He stationed the priests at their posts and strengthened them for the service of the house of the LORD.
verses.35:3: He said to the Levites who instructed all Israel and who were holy to the LORD, "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon the son of David, king of Israel, built; you have no burden on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel.
verses.35:4: Make preparations by your fathers' houses according to your divisions, in accordance with the writing of David king of Israel and the document of Solomon his son.
verses.35:5: Stand in the holy place according to the groupings of the fathers' houses of your brothers, the common people, with a division of a father's house of the Levites for each.
verses.35:6: Slaughter the Passover offering, consecrate yourselves, and make preparations for your brothers, to act according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses."
verses.35:7: Then Josiah contributed to the common people, for all who were present, lambs and young goats from the flock, all for the Passover offerings, numbering thirty thousand, and three thousand cattle; these were from the possessions of the king.
verses.35:8: His officials also contributed as a freewill offering to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the chief officers of the house of God, gave to the priests two thousand six hundred for the Passover offerings, and three hundred cattle.
verses.35:9: Conaniah also, along with Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the officials of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand for the Passover offerings, and five hundred cattle.
verses.35:10: So the service was set in order, and the priests stood in their places and the Levites in their divisions, according to the command of the king.
verses.35:11: They slaughtered the Passover offering, and the priests dashed the blood received from their hands, while the Levites did the skinning.
verses.35:12: They set aside the burnt offerings to give them to the divisions of the fathers' houses of the common people, to offer to the LORD as it is written in the book of Moses; and likewise with the cattle.
verses.35:13: They cooked the Passover offering over the fire according to the ordinance, and they cooked the holy offerings in pots, kettles, and pans, and carried them quickly to all the common people.
verses.35:14: Afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were occupied in offering up the burnt offerings and the fat portions until night; therefore the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
verses.35:15: The singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their station according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer, and the gatekeepers were at every gate. They did not need to turn aside from their service, because their brothers the Levites prepared for them.
verses.35:16: Thus all the service of the LORD was set in order on that day, to observe the Passover and to offer up burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
verses.35:17: The sons of Israel who were present observed the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
verses.35:18: No Passover like it had been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel had observed a Passover such as Josiah observed, together with the priests, the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
verses.35:19: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah this Passover was observed.
verses.35:20: After all this, when Josiah had set the house in order, Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to confront him.
verses.35:21: But he sent messengers to him, saying, "What is there between me and you, king of Judah? I am not coming against you yourself today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. Refrain from opposing God, who is with me, so that He will not destroy you."
verses.35:22: Yet Josiah did not turn his face away from him, rather he disguised himself to fight against him. He did not listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and he came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
verses.35:23: The archers shot at King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, "Remove me, for I have been gravely wounded."
verses.35:24: So his servants removed him from the chariot, placed him in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem. And he died and was buried in the tombs of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
verses.35:25: Jeremiah also uttered a lament for Josiah, and all the male and female singers have spoken about Josiah in their laments to this day. They made them an ordinance in Israel, and see, they are written in the Laments.
verses.35:26: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and his acts of loyal love, according to what is written in the law of the LORD,
verses.35:27: and his acts, from first to last, look, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
verses.36:1: And the people of the land took Jehoahaz, Josiah's son, and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem.
verses.36:2: Joahaz was twenty-three years old when he began his reign, and he reigned for three months in Jerusalem.
verses.36:3: Then the king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem and fined the land a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
verses.36:4: And the king of Egypt made his brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem, and he changed his name to Jehoiakim. As for his brother Joahaz, Neco took him and brought him into Egypt.
verses.36:5: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began his reign, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
verses.36:6: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, marched up against him and bound him in bronze shackles to lead him to Babylon.
verses.36:7: And Nebuchadnezzar brought some of the vessels of the house of the LORD to Babylon, and he placed them in his palace in Babylon.
verses.36:8: As for the rest of the deeds of Jehoiakim, and his abominations that he committed, and what was found against him, see, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. And his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
verses.36:9: Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began his reign, and he reigned for three months and ten days in Jerusalem; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.36:10: And at the return of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him to Babylon along with the treasured vessels of the house of the LORD, and he made Zedekiah, his brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.36:11: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began his reign, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem.
verses.36:12: And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God; he did not humble himself in the presence of Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
verses.36:13: Moreover, he rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had put him under oath by God, and he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart so as not to return to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.36:14: Also, all the leaders of the priests and the people multiplied their unfaithfulness according to all the abominations of the nations, and they defiled the house of the LORD that He had consecrated in Jerusalem.
verses.36:15: And the LORD, the God of their fathers, sent to them by the hand of His messengers, rising early and sending, for He felt compassion for His people and for His dwelling.
verses.36:16: But they kept ridiculing the messengers of God, and scorning His words, and deriding His prophets, until the fury of the LORD rose up against His people, until there was no healing.
verses.36:17: So He brought the king of the Chaldeans up against them, who killed their young men by the sword inside the house of their sanctuary and felt no compassion for young man or virgin, elderly or very old; all of them He gave into his hand.
verses.36:18: And all the vessels of the house of God, both large and small, together with the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king and his officials, all of it he brought to Babylon.
verses.36:19: Then they burned the house of God and tore down the wall of Jerusalem; all its citadels they burned with fire, and all its treasured vessels they destroyed.
verses.36:20: And he exiled the remnant from the sword to Babylon, and they became servants for him and for his sons until the kingdom of Persia began to reign,
verses.36:21: in order to fulfill the word of the LORD through the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had made up for its sabbaths. Throughout all the days it lay desolate, it kept sabbath, so as to fulfill seventy years.
verses.36:22: And in the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD through the mouth of Jeremiah would come to completion, the LORD roused the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, and he sent out a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying,
verses.36:23: "This is what Cyrus, king of Persia, says: 'The LORD, the God of heaven, has given all the kingdoms of the earth to me, and He Himself has commissioned me to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever among you is from all His people, may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.'"

notes.1:4: The form בַּהֵכִין combines the preposition בְּ with the article הַ functioning as a relative marker before the Hiphil perfect הֵכִין (a characteristic Late Biblical Hebrew construction), with an unexpressed antecedent ("the place").
notes.1:5: MT vocalizes שָׁם ("there") rather than שָׂם ("he placed," as in some ancient versions). The masculine singular suffix on וַיִּדְרְשֵׁהוּ ("sought it") refers to the bronze altar or tabernacle as a place of worship (cf. Deut 12:5; 1 Chr 13:3), though it can also refer to the LORD ("sought Him").
notes.1:13: MT reads לַבָּמָה ("to/at the high place," echoing v. 3) before "Jerusalem, from before the tent of meeting," whereas LXX and Vulgate read "from the high place." Here לְ is rendered locatively ("at") in relation to the tent of meeting.
notes.1:16: מִקְוֵא is understood as מִן־קְוֵא ("from Kue," ancient Cilicia in southeastern Anatolia), paralleling Egypt; the traditional Masoretic accentuation and older interpretations took מִקְוֵא as a "drove" or "company."
notes.2:2: The כַּאֲשֶׁר ("As") clause is elliptical, leaving the expected main clause ("so deal with me") unexpressed until Solomon's requests in vv. 6-7.
notes.2:8: וְהַפְלֵא is a Hiphil infinitive absolute of פלא used adjectivally or adverbially alongside גָּדוֹל ("great and wondrous").
notes.2:9: MT reads חִטִּים מַכּוֹת ("crushed" or "beaten wheat," associated with the root נכה), whereas the parallel in 1 Kgs 5:11 (MT 5:25) reads מַכֹּלֶת ("food").
notes.2:12: In לְחוּרָם אָבִי, the preposition לְ functions as a Late Biblical Hebrew direct-object marker, and אָבִי (lit. "my father") serves as an honorific title for a master craftsman (cf. 2 Chr 4:16).
notes.3:1: MT reads אֲשֶׁר הֵכִין בִּמְקוֹם דָּוִיד ("which he prepared at the place of David," with מְקוֹם in the construct state), whereas LXX and Vulgate transpose the wording to "at the place that David had prepared." The unexpressed subject of the Niphal נִרְאָה ("He had appeared") is the LORD.
notes.3:10: צַעֲצֻעִים ("sculpted work") is a biblical hapax legomenon whose exact sense is uncertain, commonly understood as carved, sculpted, or molded metalwork.
notes.3:16: MT reads בַּדְּבִיר ("in the inner sanctuary"); a commonly proposed emendation is כָּרָבִיד ("like a necklace").
notes.3:17: Ketiv הימיני vs. Qere הַיְמָנִי is an orthographic variant; both mean "the one on the right."
notes.4:3: The Masoretic Text reads 'oxen' (beqarim), differing from 'gourds' (peqa'im) in 1 Kings 7:24. The closing phrase literally reads 'cast in its casting' (Qal passive participle of yatsaq), meaning cast together in one piece with the sea.
notes.4:5: The Masoretic Text uses a double-verb capacity idiom combining the Hiphil participle of chazaq ('holding') with the Hiphil imperfect of kul ('could contain') and records three thousand baths, compared with two thousand baths in 1 Kings 7:26.
notes.4:11: Ketiv reads 'Hiram' (chiram), while the Qere followed here reads 'Huram' (churam), matching the Chronicler's usual spelling earlier in this verse and in 4:16.
notes.4:16: Hebrew literally reads 'Huram his father' (churam 'aviv; compare 'Huram my father' in 2 Chronicles 2:12), using 'father' as an honorific title for a master craftsman or chief adviser.
notes.4:21: The phrase 'the finest gold' renders the unique expression mikhlot zahav, literally 'perfections of gold' (from kalah, 'to be complete'), denoting gold of the highest purity.
notes.5:5: The Masoretic Text reads 'the Levitical priests' (literally 'the priests, the Levites') without a conjunction, differing from 'the priests and the Levites' in 1 Kings 8:4.
notes.5:9: Following the Masoretic Text strictly, the ends of the poles were visible 'from the ark' (differing from 'from the holy place' in 1 Kings 8:8), and the final verb is singular ('it is there'), referring to the ark rather than the poles.
notes.5:12: Ketiv reads a reduplicated participle form (mchtsrrym), while the Qere followed here reads machtserim, the Hiphil participle of the denominative verb chatsar ('to sound trumpets').
notes.5:13: Ketiv reads a quadriliteral participle form (lmchtstsrym), while the Qere followed here reads lamchatserim, the Piel participle of chatsar ('the trumpeters'). Verses 5:11-13 form a single suspended Hebrew period culminating in the cloud filling the house of the LORD.
notes.6:13: The Hebrew noun kiyyor normally denotes a bronze basin or laver, but here uniquely refers to a raised bronze platform or dais measuring five cubits square and three cubits high.
notes.6:22: Hebrew nasa' is an alternate spelling of nasa ('impose, lift'), used here impersonally ('an oath is imposed'). The following clause uva' 'alah is grammatically difficult and can be understood either as 'he comes under oath' (or 'comes and swears') or as 'the oath comes' before the altar.
notes.6:26: The pointed form ta'anem can be parsed either as Hiphil of the root meaning 'be afflicted' ('because You afflict them') or as Qal of 'answer' ('because You answer them'); the context of disciplinary drought favors 'afflict.'
notes.6:42: The plural construct hasde Dawid can be read objectively as 'the acts of loyal love promised to David' (cf. Isa 55:3) or subjectively as 'David's own acts of loyal love' (cf. 2 Chr 32:32; 35:26).
notes.7:3: Hebrew wehodot ('and gave thanks') is a Hiphil infinitive of the root ydh continuing the preceding narrative verb chain, a syntactic feature common in Late Biblical Hebrew.
notes.7:6: Ketiv reads a reduplicated participial form while Qere reads the Hiphil participle mahtserim from the denominative verb meaning 'sound trumpets'; both convey the same sense ('blew trumpets'), and the Qere is followed.
notes.7:18: Hebrew karatti ('I covenanted,' literally 'I cut') omits its usual object 'covenant' and forms a wordplay with the following Niphal lo'-yikkaret ('shall not be cut off').
notes.7:20: The Masoretic Text shifts from second-person plural address in verse 19 ('you yourselves') to third-person plural here ('uproot them ... gave to them'), a reading preserved directly from the Hebrew source.
notes.8:10: Ketiv/Qere variant: the Qere reads han-nitsavim (Niphal masculine plural participle of natsav, "the appointed/stationed officers"), while the Ketiv reads han-netsivim (plural noun, "the deputies/prefects"). Both denote administrative overseers.
notes.8:11: The masculine plural pronoun hemmah ("they") refers contextually to the places or precincts of David's house, and aron ("ark") is here construed as feminine with the 3fs Qal perfect ba'ah ("has come").
notes.8:16: Literally "up to the day of the founding of the house of the LORD and until its completion," using ad ... ve-ad to span both the preparatory work leading up to foundation day and construction through completion.
notes.8:18: Orthographic Ketiv/Qere variant: the Qere reads the standard spelling oniyyot ("ships"), while the Ketiv has a plene spelling with an extra vav; the meaning is identical.
notes.9:4: The Masoretic text reads aliyyato ("his ascent" or "his stairway," noun aliyyah), matching the Qal imperfect ya'aleh ("he went up"), whereas 1 Kings 10:5 and some ancient versions reflect olato ("his burnt offering") with the homographic Hiphil imperfect ya'aleh ("he offered up").
notes.9:10: Ketiv/Qere variant on the Tyrian king's name: the Qere reads Huram (Chronicles' usual spelling), while the Ketiv reads Hiram (as in Kings).
notes.9:12: Literally "beyond what she had brought to the king," an elliptical Chronicles idiom meaning Solomon gave her all she requested in addition to reciprocating beyond the gifts she had brought him.
notes.9:15: The weight unit "shekels" is implicit in the Hebrew idiom (literally "six hundred of hammered gold," and likewise "three hundred of gold" in 9:16); zahav shahut denotes beaten, hammered, or alloyed gold.
notes.9:29: Ketiv/Qere variant on the seer's name: the Qere reads Ye'do (rendered here as "Iddo," compare Iddo in 2 Chronicles 12:15 and 13:22), while the Ketiv reads Ye'di.
notes.10:10: Qotanni (literally "my small one") is traditionally understood as "my little finger," contrasted idiomatically with motnei ("waist" or "loins"); in 10:11 and 10:14 the final clause ("but I, with scorpions," referring to barbed whips) is elliptical, omitting a repeated verb.
notes.10:14: The Masoretic text of Chronicles reads the 1cs Hiphil imperfect akhbid ("I will make heavy"), whereas 1 Kings 12:14 and some ancient versions read avi hikhbid ("my father made heavy").
notes.10:16: The Masoretic text of Chronicles opens with the fronted topic ve-khol-Yisrael ("and as for all Israel") followed directly by the causal clause ("because the king did not listen to them"), lacking the verb "saw" (vayyar) present in 1 Kings 12:16.
notes.11:15: Hebrew se'irim literally means "hairy ones" or "male goats," referring here to goat-shaped idols or demonic deities (cf. Lev 17:7).
notes.11:18: Qere reads bat ("daughter of") against ketiv ben ("son of"). The Hebrew also lacks a conjunction before Abihail, leaving it open whether she was Mahalath's mother ("and of Abihail," consistent with singular verbs and pronouns in vv. 19-20) or a second wife.
notes.11:22: Hebrew ki lehamliko (literally "for to make him king," Hiphil infinitive construct of malak) is an elliptical Late Biblical Hebrew construction expressing Rehoboam's intent.
notes.11:23: Hebrew wayyish'al hamon nashim literally says "and he sought a multitude of wives" without naming an indirect object, though the context of providing for his dispersed sons suggests he sought them for his sons.
notes.12:7: Hebrew kim'at lifletah literally means "as a little for escape," indicating either a partial measure of deliverance (as qualified in v. 8) or deliverance in a short time.
notes.12:10: Hebrew haratsim literally means "the runners," a term for the royal foot-guards who escorted the king and guarded the palace entrance.
notes.12:15: Hebrew lehityaches is the Hithpael infinitive construct of yachas ("to be enrolled by genealogy"), referring here to genealogical registration or records.
notes.13:2: The Masoretic Text names Abijah's mother Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah, whereas 2 Chronicles 11:20 calls her Maacah daughter of Absalom.
notes.13:9: Hebrew lemalle yado (Piel infinitive construct of male) literally means "to fill his hand," the standard biblical idiom for priestly consecration or ordination.
notes.13:14: Ketiv preserves the fuller denominative participle with doubled tsade (from chatsotserah, "trumpet"), while qere reads the shortened Hiphil participle machtserim; both mean "sounding the trumpets."
notes.13:19: Qere reads the town name Ephrain against ketiv Ephron. Hebrew benoteha literally means "its daughters," an idiom for surrounding dependent villages.
notes.13:22: Hebrew midrash (from darash, "to inquire, study") occurs only here and in 2 Chronicles 24:27 in the Hebrew Bible, denoting an investigative record, treatise, or commentary.
notes.14:6: The Hebrew form odennu attaches a masculine singular suffix to the particle od before the feminine noun ha'aretz ("the land"), functioning neutrally as "it is still."
notes.14:8: The Hebrew expresses "one million" literally as "a thousand thousands" (elef alafim).
notes.14:10: The compact Hebrew clause ein-immekha la'zor bein rav le'ein koach uses bein...le to express "whether...or" (or "between...and"), emphasizing that only the LORD gives victory regardless of human strength. The verb atzar ("prevail") reflects Chronicles' usage meaning "retain strength" or "prevail."
notes.15:2: The Niphal verb yimmatze ("will let Himself be found") carries tolerative force, indicating God's willing response to those who seek Him; the same form recurs in 15:4 and 15:15.
notes.15:8: The Masoretic Hebrew reads literally "the prophecy, Oded the prophet" (vehannevu'ah Oded hannavi), naming Oded rather than "Azariah son of Oded" as in 15:1; the translation follows the Hebrew text without harmonizing to ancient versions.
notes.15:16: Hebrew mifletzet ("repulsive image"), from a root meaning "to shudder," refers to a loathsome cult object made for Asherah; the Hiphil verb vayyadeq ("pulverized it") specifically denotes crushing fine.
notes.16:2: The Chronicler spells Damascus as Darmeseq, an Aramaic-influenced Late Biblical Hebrew orthography.
notes.16:9: The Polel participle meshotetot ("roam") conveys continuous scanning motion, while the Hithpael infinitive lehithchazzeq ("to show Himself strong") expresses God's active display of strength for those whose heart is shalem ("whole, undivided," echoing 15:17).
notes.16:10: Hebrew beit hammahpekhet ("the house of the stocks") refers to a prison cell fitted with stocks that twisted or confined a prisoner's body.
